title: Pashchima-vibhaga. Lahari 14. The Description of Shyamananda's Branches
html:
A song in glory of Shyamananda; in separation from Shyamananda, Rasika gathers the devotees of Krishna to hold the twelfth-day festival and appoints the first aradhana in Govindapur; he tells the brothers to invite all the Shyamanandis, to decide who will be adhikari of the community and of Sri Govinda's service, and to name to him all of Shyamananda's disciples; the devotees, praising Rasika's three sons and daughter, choose his eldest son, Radhananda, full of prema for Krishna; Rasika embraces him, ties a cloth on his head and entrusts to him the service of Sri Govinda; the brothers say the Shyamanandis are countless as the waves of the ocean; the author lists Rasika's disciples — brahmanas, kings, renunciants — among them Ramakrishna, who crossed a river on a crocodile, Gokula Dasa, who manifested bhakti in Kendujhar, and Govinda Bhattacharya, who preached in Bengal, — and says they cannot be counted

The fourteenth lahari.

Raga Kaushika.1
Ghosha: "Glory, O glory to Rama and Krishna!
O Murari, O Murari, O Murari!"

1Glory, glory to Shyamananda, the purifier of the fallen,
the own dear treasure of the life of Rasika-chandra!2

2In separation from Shyamananda, Rasika-shekhara
is constantly absorbed in ecstatic feeling; [his] body is overwhelmed.3

3Taking all the devotees of Krishna, he sat to deliberate
on holding the twelfth-day festival.4

4Govindapur was fixed as the place [of the festival]:
there — the first aradhana, the great festival.5

5"This great festival [should be] known to the world;
it is fitting to bring all the communities of Shyamanandis."6

6Rasikendra says: "I know nothing —
[my] meditation and remembrance are Shyamananda's feet.

7Mad with prema for Krishna, I have spent all this time;
who lives where — I do not know them."7

8Rasika gave the command to all the brothers:
"Invite all the Shyamanandis, every one.8

9Who will be the adhikari in the Shyamanandi community?
Whom will you make [it] — deliberate on this.

10The service of Sri Govinda and the great festival —
understand that this is [a duty we have] accepted, and consider [it].9

11For I shall wander, carrying out Prabhu's work;
[arrange it] so that the service here goes on in due order.10

12Tell me the names of Shyamananda's disciples,
the disciples of [their] disciples, the servant-disciples — all who are in Utkala.11

13Kings, subjects, mahantas, all the renunciants —
who is whose disciple — distinguish them all one by one.12

14In what family each was born, where each lives —
having ascertained [this], tell of the Shyamanandi servants.13

15What love each has for Krishna,
who seeks no other refuge, who has prema-bhakti;

16who has affection for the company of sadhus, in whose heart is kindness,
who is firmly [devoted] to the guru — tell in detail.14

17Describe them to me one by one;
entrust to me the Shyamanandi community.

18I shall write to all, as befits [each];
all those people will come to the great festival."15

19All said: "Prabhu, you are detached;
you have appeared in order to give prema to the destitute.16

20Appoint one adhikari equal to yourself;
entrust to him the service of Sri Govinda."17

21Then Rasikendra gave the command to all;
Rasika, [gathering everyone] in a circle, sat to deliberate:

22"The one on whom all agree — he shall be [chosen];
quickly deliberate, come to a decision [and] bring [him]."18

23All the devotees of Krishna, gathering, deliberated:
Rasika has three sons, supremely magnanimous.

24These three brothers, born of one mother, enchant the world;
by their glance the three worlds were delivered.19

25And he has one daughter, supremely steadfast,
an abode that has taken refuge in prema for Krishna, skilled in rasa.20

26All these names and [the account of their] glory
I proclaim only to purify myself.21

27The eldest son is Radhananda, great in wisdom;
Krishnagati — [his] mind and speech are incomparable;

28[the third] is named Radhakrishna Dasa, an abode of prema for Krishna;
the daughter is named Vrindavati — she whose life is Krishna.22

29Now I shall tell the boundless glory of Radhananda —
of him to whom this authority is fitting.

30All understand only a trace of Radhananda's glory:
unceasingly [they] see his striving towards Krishna.23

31On Krishna is [his] attachment, on Krishna his mind, in Krishna his abiding;
within and without, Krishna dwells in him.

32When he falls asleep, he plays with Krishna;
when he wakes, in separation he weeps.

33Weeping and weeping, he sees the form of Radha and Krishna;
immersed, he plunges into a well of bliss.24

34At times he smiles softly, ever so slightly;
he sinks and rises in the ocean of the nectar of prema for Krishna.

35Like a blazing fire in the midst of the forest of worldly existence [is he];
seeing [him], the hordes of pashandis are consumed by burning.25

36Hunger, thirst and [the like] do not touch [his] body;
his mind, maddened with prema for Krishna, is overflowing with love.26

37He always has the strength to give Krishna and to take Krishna;
reassuring the destitute, he bestows prema.

38Feeding [a person] the fruit of prema, he fills his belly;
his grief, pain [and] burning [suffering] he reduces to ashes.

39Having eaten the fruit of prema, that one, maddened,
dances, sings, weeps, crying, "Krishna! Ha, ha, ha!"27

40All those devotees of Krishna, seeing all this,
firmly decided: he is the worthy one.

41All went and said before Rasikendra:
"Worthy to be adhikari is Radhananda, the greatly fortunate."

42They told of all his virtues;
hearing this, Prabhu was pleased, his eyes filled with tears.

43Prabhu said to all: "Call [him] and bring [him]."
All went to bring him, rejoicing.

44They told him everything in his presence;
hearing it, he was delighted, joyful at heart.28

45At the command [they] rose and quickly set out;
all the devotees of Krishna came before Prabhu.29

46Seeing Prabhu, [Radhananda] began to prostrate himself;
saying, "Rise, rise," Prabhu took [him] into his embrace.

47Embracing [him] again, Rasikendra-raya
began to speak: "Dear one, listen quickly.

48Before, you had Shyamananda's command;
now all the devotees of Krishna have surrounded you.30

49I too [give] you, dear one, this authority:
govern Shyamananda's community."31

50Prostrating himself again, he fell to the ground;
the devotees of Krishna tell Rasika to give [him] the cloth.

51With everyone's consent Rasikendra-raya
quickly tied the cloth on Radhananda's head.32

52Having tied the cloth, Rasikendra walked around [him];
with prema in his heart Prabhu says, "Hari, Hari!"

53He entrusted the service of Sri Govinda to Radhananda;
earnestly he told [him] to preach prema-bhakti.33

54Then Rasikendra again, to everyone,
spoke sweet words with love:

55"All of you, devotees of Krishna, are supremely magnanimous;
you are able to give bhakti for Krishna to all and to receive [it].34

56Count the names of the Shyamanandi Vaishnavas
and bring [them to me], dear ones, with care."

57Hearing Rasika's command, the brothers say:
"The communities of the Shyamanandis cannot be told.35

58The Shyamanandis are like the waves of the ocean;
the devotees of Krishna, the Shyamanandis, cannot be counted.

59We shall name the chief ones in [your] presence;
all together will tell what they know, as is fitting."

60Before, I described the disciples of Shyamananda;
now I shall tell of his disciples, servants [and their] disciples.

61Briefly I shall relate something about them;
all you Shyamanandis, devotees of Krishna, listen attentively.36

62Motionless, Prabhu, the son of Achyuta, listens;
with great joy all the devotees of Krishna listen.

63At the beginning of the book I offered all the obeisances:
all the disciples of Shyamananda I [named] one by one.

64Now the brothers earnestly tell of the disciples;
the son of Achyuta listens [to them] with undivided mind.37

65I shall tell in detail of Rasika's worthy disciples,
praising the firmness of each one's bhakti, such as it is.

66The first disciple is the brahmana Kalandi Bhaktadasa,
whose true abode is Rasika's feet.38

67Sri Shyamagopala Dasa, very pure of mind,
for whom Rasika-shekhara is lineage, character and caste.

68He is the son of Kashinatha, renowned in the world,
very eloquent, intelligent, one who says what is fitting.

69His mother, Govindadasi, is Rasika's servant;
by Rasika's mercy [she] is renowned [for knowing] the truth about the Vaishnavas.39

70In a village called Sri Jangha, a truly divine place,
lived a fortunate [man] named Ramadasa.

71His wife, named Draupadi, was devoted to her husband;
she was born in the clan of the shishta-karanas, renowned [to all].40

72From her womb was born Dinashyama Dasa;
from childhood Rasika was manifest in his heart.41

73The disciple of Rasika, an embodiment of prema:
whatever Rasika commands, he unfailingly does.

74Night and day he always meditates on Rasikendra;
at Rasika's feet he offered [his] caste [and] life.

75He made many disciples in the land of Utkala;
all the elders honour [him] as equal to a guru.

76Dinashyama Dasa is very dear to the Vaishnavas;
he always delights in the pastimes of prema for Krishna.

77He brought much joy upon the earth;
giving prema-bhakti to all, he delivered [them].

78The glory of Dinashyama cannot be told —
of him to whom [Rasika] entrusted his own prema-bhakti.

79The brahmana Ramakrishna Dasa, very pure of mind,
who has no other goal than Rasikendra,

80made many disciples in the land of Utkala;
all people sing of him as the blessing of the world.

81For sport he sits on the backs of tigers and crocodiles;
by Rasika's mercy he fears no one.

82Mounting a crocodile, he crosses the river —
Ramakrishna Mahashaya, the deliverer of the fallen.42

83Rasika's disciple is the renowned Narayana Dasa;
pure of heart, he knows no one but Krishna.

84The brahmana Paramananda, very pure of heart,
by Rasika's mercy became a great scholar.

85In a brahmana family was born Goura-gopala;
he knows nothing but Rasikendra.43

86The brahmana Gopinatha, a renunciant mahashaya,
in whose heart Rasikendra [abides] unceasingly,

87knows nothing but prema-bhakti for Krishna;
all his time was spent with Rasika.

88Krishna's meals, offerings of six tastes,
Gopinatha, pure in conduct, cooks.44

89Prema-ankura Dasa is Rasika's servant;
among his servants and [his] servants' servants the kadamba blossomed.45

90Rasika's disciple from childhood, Sri Gokula Dasa,
manifested bhakti in the land of Kendujhar.

91In the forest land the mahashaya made many disciples;
they know nothing but Rasikendra.46

92Shyama-manohara Dasa, very pure of mind,
who has no other goal than Rasika's feet —

93earlier I made his greatness known;
a great scholar, he delivered all people.47

94Maharaja Vaidyanatha is a great mahajana;
with body, mind and words he firmly takes refuge in Rasika.

95He left his body in the land of Utkala;
in Vrindavana he saw all the sadhus.48

96Chhota-raya [and] Rautra are very pure of mind;
they have no other goal than Rasikendra.

97Both are very mighty, embodiments of prema;
seeing their deeds, all attained bhakti.49

98Shyamadasa [and] Mohana are Prabhu's own servants;
with the songs of Jayadeva they enchant everyone.50

99The brahmana Govinda Bhattacharya Mahashaya,
in whose heart Rasikendra-chandra always [abides],

100preached bhakti for Hari in Vanga;
hundreds and hundreds of brahmanas became his disciples.51

101Rasika's disciple is the fortunate brahmana Dube:
he knows nothing other than Rasikendra-chandra.

102Tarkalankara Bhattacharya Shyamasundara —
he to whom Rasika-shekhara gave prema-bhakti.

103Rasika's disciple is the brahmana Sundara-raya,
a mahashaya, prema-bhakti for Krishna embodied.52

104The best of brahmanas, the renunciant Sri Mohana Dasa,
from birth lived together with Rasika.

105Leaving house, wife, sons, all his family,
the son of Rama went around [the whole] earth.53

106Rasika's servant is Mangaraja Harichandana;
Gopinatha Dasa Pattanayaka is a mahajana.54

107Radhavinoda Dasa, Kalandi Bhagavan,
Paramananda, Manohara, Kanu, Krishnanama,

108Krishnacharana, the brahmana Achyuta, Shricharana,
Gokulananda, Govinda — those who took refuge in Rasika.55

109The brahmana Govinda Dasa, Rasika's servant —
with prema for Krishna, night and day his body is overwhelmed.

110Rasika's disciple is Kalandi, the best of brahmanas,
whose true home is Rasika's feet.

111Akrura, Gopala, Hari, Sri Tulasi-dasi,
Raja Mitra, Chitrasena, Suvarna Vayasi.56

112The brahmana Govinda Dasa, Krishnabhakta Dasa,
Vrajamohana, the brahmana Shyamamohana Dasa.

113Sri Gopala Acharya, Kalandi Dharambara,
in whose heart unceasingly is the best one, Rasikendra;

114his sons — Radhamohana, Bhudhara,
Sri Radhagovinda, Radhakrishna, the best of brahmanas —

115with all their family became Rasika's disciples;
they know nothing but Rasikendra.57

116Great in steadfastness, an embodiment of prema, Sri Govinda Dasa,
a disciple of Rasika, lives in Ghantashila.

117He made many disciples in the land of Bhanjabhum;
he especially flooded [it] with prema for Krishna.58

118Rasika's disciple is Gangadasa Mahashaya,
an embodiment of prema, the son of Shridhara;

119Daityari, Shyamasundara, Shyamamohana,
Shyamadasa, Bhagavan — six brothers.

120All [of them] are Rasika's nephews, his servants;
for them Rasikendra-raya is caste, life [and] wealth.59

121Vrindavana-kishora is Rasika's servant;
together with [his] community he spoke [of] Krishna-tattva.60

122Chintamani [and] Vihari are very fortunate:
for them Rasikendra-chudamani is caste, wealth [and] life.61

123Achyuta, Shyamakishora, Vrindavana Dasa,
Shrirama, Bali, Vamana, Jagu, Shyamadasa.62

124All Rasika's disciples seek no other refuge;
unceasingly [they] serve the guru, Krishna and the sadhus.

125Ghanashyama Dasa, Sri Beraya Vishnudasa,
in whose hearts Rasika's feet are manifest.63

126Bahubalindra, Sri Shyama, Rasika Dasa,
Chandra, Bhanu and others are Rasika's own servants.64

127The brahmana Gopimohana, Shyamamohana Dasa,
in whose hearts Rasika's feet dwell.

128Vrajamohana, the renunciant Shyamarasika,
Sakhishyama, Gokula — very experienced.65

129In the land of Hijli is Vaikuntha Dasa Mahashaya,
in whose heart is Rasikendra-chudamani.

130Unceasingly he serves hundreds and hundreds of sadhus;
selling himself, [he] is firm in the service of the sadhus.66

131Lala, Purushottama, Shyamakishora, Yugala,
Akrura, Shyamasundara, Vamshi, Manohara.67

132Sadashiva Pattanayaka, the sadhu Uddanda,
Krishnananda Harichandana — very formidable.68

133The brahmana Jivadasa Bhunya, Raghunatha Dasa,
Krishnadasa Bhunya and others are Rasika's servants.69

134Gajendra, Mathuradasa are very pure of mind;
they have no other goal than Rasikendra.

135Madhusudana, Dvarakananda Mahashaya,
in whose heart Rasikendra [abides] unceasingly.

136Raja Ramachandra, Chitreshvara, Sri Chandana —
all with body, mind and words take refuge in Rasika.

137Madho, Manohara, Niranjana Mahashaya;
Uddhava, Hari, Keshava — the sons of Bhima.70

138Shyamasundara, Vrindavana — the sons of Vamshi;
all with their whole being take refuge in Rasika.71

139The brahmana Radhavallabha, the son of Purushottama;
princes are Rasika's disciples, crowd upon crowd.

140The two — Radhavallabha [and] Shyamadasa:
in Gahamagarh [they have] hundreds of thousands of disciples.72

141The brahmana Shyamasundara is a very great mahajana:
he cooks the bhoga for Krishna at Rasika's.73

142The brahmana Radhamohana, Uddhava, Bhagavan,
Nilambara, Vanamali, Ramadasa, Shyama.

143Krishnananda Bhunya is very pure of mind:
for him Rasika's feet are lineage, character and caste.

144Gopala Bhunya, Krishnananda Harichandana,
Gopala, Madhava, Raja Keshobanai.74

145The brahmana Sri Radhamohana is a great scholar,
Rasika's disciple, full of prema, with an intoxicated heart.

146Radhavallabha Dasa, the son of Vallabha,
is Rasika's servant, and also Vrindavana Dasa.75

147Radhamadhava, Shyamasundara, Anuraga;
Rasika's disciple is Vanamali, the greatly fortunate.

148Mukunda, Paramananda, Kanu, Bhagavan,
Agata, Mohana and others — servants, as is attested.76

149Gangadasa, Keshava and others, Sri Chandrashekhara,
Shyamasundara, Vrajamohana — the best of brahmanas.

150Radhamohana, Bhaktadasa, Purushottama,
Shyamadasa who lives under a tree, Vrajamohana.77

151Akrura, Mohanananda, Nandana, Balaka,
Manohara, Sri Radhavinoda — manifest before the eyes.78

152Krishnananda, Krishna-jivana, Bhudhara,
Sri Gopala Dasa, Radhacharana, Akrura.

153Mohana, Vrajamohana, Shyamadasa and others,
Yadava, Shyamamohana — greatly renowned.

154Sri Vinoda Dasa, Chintamani Dasa — famous,
expert in music, very, very [skilled in] poetry.79

155The brahmana Sri Murali Dasa, the brahmana Sri Gopala;
disciples of Rasika — Dvijadasa, Sri Dayala.80

156Shyamadasa, Harinarayana Mahashaya,
in whose heart is Rasikendra-chudamani.

157The brahmana Gopimohana Dasa, Shyamamohana,
the brahmana Yadunatha — people dear to Rasika.

158Nilashyama Dasa, Gopimohana, Akrura,
Ghanashyama, Ramadasa, Govinda — a brahmana.81

159Jayadeva Dasa, Laichhana, Krishnadasa,
Sri Viravara Deu, Shankara, Kanudasa.82

160Sri Govinda Bhanja, Jagannatha, Krishnadasa,
Shyama Bhanja, Telai, Shripati, Ramadasa.

161Mithi Bhanja with [his whole] community, Gopala Bhanja-raya,
Shyamadasa, Kishora and Madha-raya.83

162Radhakrishna Dasa is Rasika's own servant.
[Among] women — throng upon throng of disciples, beyond measure.84

163Rasika's servants are [like] the waves of the ocean:
who has such power as to count [them]?

164I have considered ten or twenty principal ones
[and] briefly named a few — those whose names I know.

165Behind each name are hundreds and hundreds of disciples;
there is no counting all of Rasika's disciples.85

166Now I shall tell briefly of the brothers' disciples —
the disciples, the disciples' disciples, the servant-disciples — one by one.86

167In the Pashchima-vibhaga I have proclaimed this —
whatever the son of Achyuta makes me speak.87

168Rasika's disciples seek no other refuge;
taking refuge in them, one obtains the treasure of prema for Krishna.88

169I have made the "Rasika-mangala" known a little;
listen, all, attentively, filled with joy.

170Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

Thus in the Pashchima-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the fourteenth lahari, called "The Description of Shyamananda's Branches."89

Notes

  1. The lines before the raga are the title of the lahari ("চতুর্দ্দশ-লহরী"), in italics without a number. Lahari 14 begins. Raga Kaushika (kauśika; Purva, lahari 3, note 1). The ghosha — jaẏa re jaẏa rāmakṛṣṇa murāre, o murāre o murāre — is the same as in Purva, lahari 3: Rama and Krishna are Balarama and Krishna; Murari ("the enemy of Mura") is a name of Krishna which the author also applies to Rasika-Murari. There is no mangala-shloka: after the raga and ghosha the song begins with ॥ 1 ॥. The title follows the colophon: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-পশ্চিম-বিভাগে শ্যামানন্দ-শাখাবর্ণন-নাম চতুর্দ্দশ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" (śyāmānanda-śākhā-barṇana) — "The Description of Shyamananda's Branches": the "branches" are disciples and their disciples (cf. the branches of the Chaitanya tree, CC Adi 10–12). The summary line covers the whole lahari.
  2. "The purifier of the fallen" — patita-pābana. "The own dear treasure of the life" — nija priẏa prāṇadhana: Shyamananda is Rasika's guru. On the author's attitude to Shyamananda and Rasika, see Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11.
  3. "Absorbed in ecstatic feeling" — bhābābeśe. "Overwhelmed" — jara jara (Pashchima, lahari 12, note 16).
  4. "The twelfth-day festival" — duẏādaśa mahotsaba (duẏādaśa = dbādaśa): apparently a festival in memory of the departed held on the twelfth day after his departure; it may also be understood as "twelve festivals." "Devotees of Krishna" — kārṣṇajana (Purva, lahari 10, note 13).
  5. Govindapur — cf. Sri Govindapur (lahari 13, 15, 19; note 8). "Was fixed" — karila niścaẏa; the subject is not expressed (Rasika with the devotees). "The first aradhana" — ādya ārādhanā: apparently the first festival in Shyamananda's memory (on the aradhana festival, lahari 13, note 8). 5 is taken as Rasika's words (cf. 6).
  6. "It is fitting to bring" — ānibā ucita. "Communities" — goṣṭhī (Pashchima, lahari 12, note 20).
  7. "Meditation and remembrance" — dhyāna saṅaraṇa (saṅaraṇa = smaraṇa). "I have spent all this time" — gela eta kāle, "so much time has passed": absorbed in prema, Rasika does not know all of Shyamananda's disciples or where they live.
  8. "The brothers" — bhāigaṇe: apparently godbrothers, disciples of Shyamananda. "Every one" — sarbajane.
  9. "Adhikari" (9) — adhikārī: a successor, the head of the community, to whom the service of the Deity is entrusted (cf. 20, 29). 10b — ihā aṅgīkṛta bujhi kara anubhaba: the sense is approximate.
  10. "Carrying out Prabhu's work" — prabhukārya anbeṣiẏā, literally "seeking out Prabhu's work": Shyamananda's mission. "In due order" — subandhāna haña, "being well arranged."
  11. "The disciples of [their] disciples, the servant-disciples" — anuśiṣya bhṛtyaśiṣya (Pashchima, lahari 12, note 17).
  12. "Mahantas" — mohānta, abbots, teachers. "Renunciants" — udāsīna, detached wanderers. "Distinguish one by one" — kara bhinna bhinna.
  13. "Tell of the Shyamanandi servants" — kaha śyāmānandī dāsa; it may also be understood as an address: "tell, O Shyamanandi servants."
  14. "Love" (15) — suprīti. "Seeks no other refuge" — ananya-śaraṇa. "Firmly [devoted] to the guru" — gurute niścita.
  15. "Entrust to me the community" (17) — goṣṭhī more kara samarpaṇa: apparently "hand over to me [the list of] the community." "I shall write" — kariba lekhana: apparently he will send letters of invitation.
  16. "Detached" — udāsa: Rasika does not cling to the world (cf. his wish to wander, 11). "You have appeared" — haẏecha prakāśa: the disciples speak of Rasika as one who has appeared in the world for the sake of mercy; on the author's attitude to Rasika, see Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11. "The destitute" — akiñcane, "those who have nothing."
  17. "Equal to yourself" — ātmatulya. The service of Sri Govinda — of the Deity of Sri Govinda in Gopivallabhapur (Pashchima, lahari 11).
  18. 21b — rasika maṇḍalī kari basila bicāre: understood as "Rasika, [gathering everyone] in a circle, sat to deliberate"; it may also be understood as "the rasikas, forming a circle, sat to deliberate." 22 is taken as Rasika's words: sabāre sammata yā're sei paramāṇa / tbarāẏa bicāri āna kari anumāna; āna — "bring" (cf. 43); "come to a decision" — kari anumāna.
  19. Rasika's sons are Radhananda, Krishnagati and Radhakrishnadasa (27–28; Purva, lahari 1, 110, 122, 124, note 48; Dakshina, lahari 11, note 24). "Born of one mother" — sahodara. "By their glance the three worlds were delivered" — yāhāra kaṭākṣe uddhārila tribhubana: the author's rapturous praise.
  20. The daughter is named in 28: Vrindavati (Purva, lahari 1, 121). "An abode that has taken refuge in prema for Krishna" — kṛṣṇapremāśrita-dhāma. "Skilled in rasa" — rasika-caturā; it may also be understood as "skilled [in serving] Rasika."
  21. "[The account of their] glory" — mahimā bicāra. "To purify myself" — āpanā śodhite.
  22. 27b — kṛṣṇagatimati kathā ati anupama: understood as "Krishnagati — [his] mind and speech are incomparable," i.e. the middle son (Purva, lahari 1, 122); it may also be read as praise of Radhananda: "whose mind is set on Krishna, whose speech is incomparable." The author calls Radhananda the eldest, although Rasika's first-born was Vrajananda (Dakshina, lahari 11, note 18). Radhakrishna Dasa is Radhakrishnadasa (Purva, lahari 1, 124). "Daughter" — sutā.
  23. "Unceasingly" — abacchinne. "Striving towards Krishna" — kṛṣṇera uddeśa, "seeking of Krishna"; the subject of "see" is taken as "all" (30a).
  24. "The form of Radha and Krishna" — rādhākṛṣṇa-rūpe. "A well of bliss" — ānandera kūpe.
  25. "The forest of worldly existence" — bhabāṭabī. Pashandis (pāṣaṇḍī) — unbelievers, opponents of bhakti. "Are consumed by burning" — jbaliẏā mare, literally "burning, they perish": the pashandis cannot bear his radiance (the metaphor of fire).
  26. "Overflowing with love" — gara gara rāge.
  27. "To give Krishna and to take Krishna" (37) — kṛṣṇa dite kṛṣṇa nite. "The fruit of prema" — premaphala. "His," "that one" (38–39) — tā'ra, se: the one to whom Radhananda gives prema. "Ha, ha, ha!" — hā hā hā, cries of longing.
  28. "In his presence" — tā̃'ra bidyamāne: Radhananda was told of the decision.
  29. "Devotees of Krishna" — kārṣṇagaṇa, kārṣṇajana, as in 3 and 23 (note 4). The subject of "rose" is Radhananda and those who had come for him (43–44). "Prabhu" here and below is Rasika.
  30. "Have surrounded you" — beṣṭilā: apparently "have agreed upon you, chosen you" (40–41).
  31. "Govern" — nibāra karaha; understood as nirbāha, "management, administration"; the reading is unclear. "Community" — maṇḍalī. "Authority" — adhikāra (note 9).
  32. "Cloth" — śāṛī: here apparently a head-cloth (turban), a sign of succession, as Shyamananda tied a cloth on Rasika (lahari 13, 43, note 20). Radhananda is Rasika's eldest son (27; Purva, lahari 1, 110, note 48).
  33. The service of Sri Govinda — note 17 (cf. 10, 20).
  34. kṛṣṇabhakti dite nite pāra sabākāra: may also be understood as "you are able to give bhakti for Krishna to all and to take [it] from all."
  35. "The brothers" — bhāigaṇa (note 8). "Cannot be told" — nā yāẏa kathana. 57b–59 are the brothers' words.
  36. "Before, I described" — in the Purva-vibhaga, lahari 1, 46–145 (cf. 63). "His disciples, servants [and their] disciples" — tā'ra śiṣya-bhṛtya-śiṣyagaṇe: apparently the second generation — Rasika's disciples and their disciples (note 11; cf. below, 166: śiṣya anuśiṣya bhṛtyaśiṣya). The speaker in 60–61 is apparently the author (cf. 63), though the words may also be ascribed to the brothers (57–59). "Briefly" — saṃkṣepe.
  37. ebe bhāigaṇa śiṣya kahiye yugate: may also be understood as "now, brothers, I shall tell of the disciples" (an address) or "now I shall tell of the brothers' disciples" (cf. lahari 15, 2). "Earnestly" — yugate (Dakshina, lahari 4, note 6). "With undivided mind" — eka mane.
  38. Kalandi (kālandī) is apparently a surname (of a family?), not a separate name: cf. "Kalandi Bhagavan" (107), "Kalandi, the best of brahmanas" (110), "Kalandi Dharambara" (113); in Dakshina, lahari 4 (note 8), "Kalandi" and "Bhaktadasa the yavana" were taken as two disciples. "First" — ādya. "True abode" — nijabāsa, "own dwelling."
  39. Shyamagopala is a disciple of Rasika (Purva, lahari 1, 131; Dakshina, lahari 4, note 8; Pashchima, lahari 1, note 19). Kashinatha is apparently Kashinatha Dasa, Rasika's elder brother (Dakshina, lahari 3, note 22); Shyamagopala would then be Rasika's nephew. "One who says what is fitting" — ye kahe ucitā. 69b — rasika kṛpāẏa khyāta baiṣṇabera tattba: the sense is approximate; it may also be understood as "[he] by Rasika's mercy is renowned [for knowing] the truth about the Vaishnavas."
  40. Sri Jangha — śrījaṃha: the village is unidentified, the reading unclear. Draupadi is Dinashyama's mother (72). The shishta-karanas (śiṣṭakaraṇa) are a subdivision of the karana (scribe) caste of Utkala (cf. Purva, lahari 3, note 23).
  41. Dinashyama — Purva, lahari 1, 132; Pashchima, lahari 7, 13, note 10. "All the elders honour [him] as equal to a guru" (75) — guru-tulya mānya kare saba gurujane. "Pastimes of prema" (76) — premera bilāsa. 78b — nija premabhakti yā're kaila samarpaṇa: the subject is not expressed; understood as Rasika; it may also be understood as "[Dinashyama], who entrusted his own prema-bhakti [to people]."
  42. Ramakrishna — Purva, lahari 1, 132; Pashchima, lahari 7, 13. "Blessing of the world" (80) — bhubana-maṅgala. "For sport" — kutūhale. The author ascribes the fearlessness before tigers and crocodiles to the guru's mercy (rasika-kṛpāẏa).
  43. Goura-gopala — Dakshina, lahari 4, note 8.
  44. "Six tastes" — ṣaṛarasa (Dakshina, lahari 3, note 7). "Pure in conduct" — sadācāra.
  45. Prema-ankura (prema-aṅkura, "sprout of prema") is taken as a name. "The kadamba blossomed" — kadamba phuṭāla: the kadamba flower is a traditional figure for hair standing on end in ecstatic love (pulaka); a play on the name: among his servants and his servants' servants the "sprout of prema" came into bloom. The sense is approximate.
  46. Gokula — Purva, lahari 1, 82; Dakshina, lahari 4, note 8. "Disciple from childhood" — bālya śiṣya. Kendujhar (kendujhuri) is apparently Keonjhar, a principality in northern Utkala. "In the forest land" — banabhūme, Vanabhumi (Dakshina, lahari 2, note 10; Dakshina, lahari 8).
  47. Shyama-manohara, formerly Vishvanatha Bhunya; on his initiation and glory see Dakshina, lahari 10, 44–66 (notes 22, 26).
  48. Maharaja Vaidyanatha is apparently Raja Vaidyanatha Bhanja (Dakshina, lahari 12, note 10; Pashchima, lahari 7). "Left his body" — dehatyāga karilena. 95b — bṛndābane dekhilena saba sādhugaṇe: apparently, having left his body, he attained Vrindavana, Krishna's eternal abode, and saw all the saints there; the sense is approximate.
  49. Chhota-raya and Rautra are the younger brothers of Raja Vaidyanatha (Dakshina, lahari 12, 17, note 10). "Both" — dõhe: this confirms that they are two persons. "Very mighty" — baṛai pratāpī. "Deeds" — karaṇī.
  50. "Shyamadasa [and] Mohana" — śyāmadāsa mohana; possibly one person. "Prabhu" is Rasika. The songs of Jayadeva — the Gita-govinda.
  51. Govinda Bhattacharya, who preached in Vanga, is also named in the Purva-vibhaga (lahari 1, 102), there among Shyamananda's disciples. Vanga — East Bengal (Purva, lahari 1, note 45).
  52. Dube (dube) is a brahmana surname (dbibedī); the given name is not stated. Tarkalankara (tarkālaṅkāra, "ornament of logic") is a scholarly title. "The brahmana Sundara-raya" — dbijasundara se rāẏa; it may also be taken as the name "Dvijasundara-raya."
  53. The edition's footnote gives a variant for 104b: bilāsa instead of nibāsa ("from birth delighted [in the company] of Rasika"). "The son of Rama" — rāmera kumāra: apparently Mohana Dasa is the son of a certain Rama; unidentified. "Went around [the whole] earth" — pṛthbī-parikramā: pilgrimage to the holy places.
  54. Mangaraja, Harichandana, Pattanayaka are Oriya titles of the nobility and of the karanas (Dakshina, lahari 5, note 13; Purva, lahari 3, note 23). Understood: Mangaraja Harichandana is one person.
  55. The division of the list in 107–108 is uncertain. Kalandi — note 38. "Krishnanama" (kṛṣṇanāma) is taken as a name; it may also be understood as "Kanu, [whose name is] Krishna." "Those who took refuge in Rasika" — rasikaśaraṇa; possibly also a name, Rasikasharana.
  56. Sri Tulasi-dasi (śrītulasī dāsī) is apparently a woman. The division of the second line is unclear: rājā mitra citrasena subarṇa baẏasī; "Vayasi" (baẏasī) may mean "contemporary, companion": "Suvarna, [their] companion." Taken as names.
  57. Dharambara, Radhamohana, Bhudhara — cf. Purva, lahari 1, 80–81, 100. "His sons" — tā̃hāra nandana: understood as the sons of Gopala Acharya (or of Kalandi Dharambara, if this is one person).
  58. Ghantashila — ghaṇṭaśilā; the edition's footnote gives the variant thuṇṭāpāre. Bhanjabhum — bhañjabhũi deśa, "the land of the Bhanjas" (Dakshina, lahari 16, note 5). "Flooded" — ḍhalāḍhali karila (lahari 13, note 18).
  59. Shridhara is apparently Rasika's brother: his six sons are "Rasika's nephews" (rasika bhrātuṣputra, brother's sons). A Shridhara is named in the Purva list (lahari 1, 129); Rasika's elder brother is Kashinatha (note 39). The six brothers are Gangadasa, Daityari, Shyamasundara, Shyamamohana, Shyamadasa, Bhagavan.
  60. "Together with [his] community" — sagoṣṭhī sahite. "Spoke [of] Krishna-tattva" — balilena kṛṣṇatattba: he preached the truth about Krishna.
  61. Chintamani and Vihari — Purva, lahari 1, 131. Rasikendra-chudamani is an epithet of Rasika (Purva, lahari 1, note 59).
  62. "Bali" (bali) is taken as a name (cf. "Vamana"); it may also be understood as "named": "named Shrirama" (as baliẏā in 70). Jagu — jagu; the edition's footnote gives the variant jaẏa.
  63. "Beraya" — beṛaẏā: apparently a surname (from a village?); unidentified.
  64. Bahubalindra (bāhubalīndra) is apparently an Oriya title of the nobility (bāhubalendra); taken as a name or surname. The division "Sri Shyama, Rasika Dasa" is uncertain: possibly "Sri Shyamarasika Dasa."
  65. Sakhishyama — sakhīśyāma; the edition's footnote gives the variant duḥkhīśyāma ("Duhkhishyama"). "Very experienced" — baṛai prabīṇa.
  66. Hijli (hijalī maṇḍala) — a coastal tract in south-eastern Medinipur (Purva, lahari 10, note 21). "Selling himself" — āpanā bikāñā: giving himself wholly to the service of the sadhus.
  67. "Yugala" (yugala, "pair") is taken as a name; it may be understood as "the two — Lala [and] Purushottama" or "Shyamakishora [with] his pair."
  68. "The sadhu Uddanda" — sādhu uddaṇḍa; it may also be understood as "the unrestrained sadhu" (an epithet of Sadashiva); cf. Uddanda-raya of Nrisimhapur (lahari 13, note 15) — the person is unidentified. Harichandana, Pattanayaka — note 54. "Formidable" — pracaṇḍa.
  69. Bhunya (bhuñā) — a bhuiyan, a landholder (Dakshina, lahari 10, note 22; Dakshina, lahari 12, note 7). The division of 133a is uncertain; understood as "Jivadasa Bhunya" on the pattern of "Krishnadasa Bhunya" (133b, cf. 143–144); it may also be "Bhunya Raghunatha Dasa."
  70. Chitreshvara, Sri Chandana are unidentified. "The sons of Bhima" — bhīmera tanaẏa: apparently refers to Uddhava, Hari and Keshava (or "Harikeshava" is one name). Bhima is unidentified.
  71. Vamshi is possibly Vamshi, the author's uncle (Purva, lahari 1, 137, note 57; Dakshina, lahari 4, note 14); unidentified. "With their whole being" — sarbātmabhābete.
  72. "Princes" — nṛpasuta, "sons of kings." "Crowd upon crowd" — yūtha yūtha. Gahamagarh is unidentified. "Hundreds of thousands" — lakṣa lakṣa.
  73. "The bhoga for Krishna at Rasika's" — rasikera kṛṣṇabhoga: the food that Rasika offers to Krishna.
  74. "Raja Keshobanai" — keśobanāi rājana: the reading and division are unclear; possibly "Kesho, Banai, the raja."
  75. "The son of Vallabha" — ballabhanandana: apparently Radhavallabha, the author's son (son of Gopijana-vallabha; Purva, lahari 1, 142, note 59).
  76. "Anuraga" (anurāga, "love") is taken as a name. "Agata" — āgaṭa: unidentified. "As is attested" — paramāṇa, "[such is] the evidence."
  77. The division of the list into names here and below (150–162) is conjectural; most of the persons are unidentified (cf. note 55). "Who lives under a tree" — gāchataliẏā: apparently Shyamadasa's byname — a hermit living under trees (cf. gāchatalā, "the foot of a tree"); it may also be a byname from a village Gachhtala.
  78. 151a — akrūra mohanānanda nandana bālaka: "Nandana, Balaka" are taken as names; it can also be read "Akrura, the young son (nandana bālaka) of Mohanananda." "Manifest before the eyes" — pratyakṣa, "visible, evident"; the sense is unclear (perhaps "known in person," "now living").
  79. "Sri Vinoda Dasa" — dāsa śrībinoda (the word order is for the metre). "Expert in music" — saṅgīta biśārada; it may refer to Chintamani Dasa alone (cf. Chintamani, 122; Purva, lahari 1, 78). "Very, very [skilled in] poetry" — baṛa baṛai kabitā, literally "great, very great poetry"; the sense is approximate.
  80. dbijadāsa śrīdaẏāla: "Dvijadasa" is taken as a name; it can also be read "the brahmana Dasa Sri Dayala" (cf. dbija before names in 155a, 157).
  81. "A brahmana" — bhūsura, "a god on earth"; it apparently refers to Govinda, but may refer to all named in 158.
  82. Laichhana — cf. Loichhana Parichha (lahari 15, 11). Deu (deu) is an Oriya title (= deba, "deva"); taken as "Sri Viravara Deu," one person.
  83. Bhanja (Govinda Bhanja, Shyama Bhanja, Mithi Bhanja, Gopala Bhanja-raya) — the family of the rajas of Mayurbhanj (Purva, lahari 1, note 49; Bhanjabhum — note 58); the persons are unidentified. Telai (telāi; cf. Tilai, lahari 15, 52) is unidentified. "With [his whole] community" — sagoṣṭhī, with all his kin. Madha-raya — mādharāẏa, apparently = Madhava-raya.
  84. strīri: the reading is unclear; taken as "among women" (strī): among Rasika's disciples there are also women (cf. the women disciples in lahari 15, 71–74). "Throng upon throng" — yūtha yūtha. "Beyond measure" — apramita.
  85. "The waves of the ocean" — cf. 58. "I have considered" — kariluṃ bicāra. "Those whose names I know" — kichu nāma jāni yā'ra. 163–165 are the author's words (or the brothers', cf. 57–59).
  86. "The brothers" — bhāigaṇa (note 8): Shyamananda's disciples, Rasika's spiritual brothers. "The disciples, the disciples' disciples, the servant-disciples" — śiṣya anuśiṣya bhṛtyaśiṣya (note 11). The promise is fulfilled in lahari 15 (2, 25, 42–43).
  87. "The son of Achyuta" — acyuta-kumāra, Rasika (lahari 13, note 34). "Makes me speak" — bolāẏa more: the author ascribes his words to Rasika. On the author's view of Shyamananda and Rasika — Purva, lahari 1, note 2; Purva, lahari 14, note 11.
  88. "Taking refuge in them" — yāhāra śaraṇe, "in whose refuge." "Seek no other refuge" — ananyaśaraṇa (note 14).
  89. The author's signature (170) and the colophon are: "ইতি শ্রীরসিকমঙ্গল-পশ্চিম-বিভাগে শ্যামানন্দ-শাখাবর্ণন-নাম চতুর্দ্দশ-লহরী সম্পূর্ণা" — the title agrees with the heading (note 1).
